description: Fetch specifications as a tree, in one of four modes. Default: the subtree rooted at `id`. `branch`: a single chain from the top-level ancestor down to `id`, which is the deepest node. `query`: ranked search matches (at most 20) nested with their ancestors in one call, so there is no need to walk specs_list; `id` optionally scopes matches to its direct children; a match's `snippet` holds the matched text when the server found the match by meaning, and is otherwise null or absent; if a query finds little, retry with other wording. `executionOrder`: the unfiltered subtree under `id` plus the order in which its leaves can be implemented and the blockers holding them back. Only prepared/processing leaves are planned; draft leaves count as unprepared blockers. A root without children is its own only candidate, so call it on a leaf to get that leaf's blockers. Leaves inherit blockers from their ancestors up to and including the root. A cycle yields an empty order instead of an error. The result is a consistent one-time snapshot. `status` (draft | prepared | processing | completed) prunes branches without a matching node. Mode rules (errors use CLI flags): --execution-order requires an id and cannot combine with --branch, --query or --status; --query and --branch are exclusive and the query must not be empty; --branch cannot combine with --status. Returns an array of nodes, or `{tree, plan}` with executionOrder.

id.description: Root specification id (optional only in query mode).

status.description: Keep nodes with this status or a matching descendant (CLI: --status).

name: specs_tree
title: Specification tree
